for International students When planning your studies, it’s important to consider additional costs. You will need to pay a portion of your tuition fees as a deposit once you have accepted your place on your course. You will be advised of the deposit value for your chosen course during your application. This payment will secure your place. You can then pay the remaining amount of your fees in full or in instalments. Tuition fees: Our tuition fees are: Undergraduate top-up: £16,000 Postgraduate: £17,500 With our introductory offer this is reduced to: Undergraduate top-up: £13,000 in London and £12,000 in Manchester Postgraduate: £13,500 in London and £12,500 in Manchester. Find out more on our scholarships page Terms and conditions apply Programme-specific fees are available on our fees and funding page . You can choose to pay for your studies in full or enter a payment plan to pay in instalments for each year of study. This can be arranged with your student recruitment advisor prior to your enrolment. Accommodation fees: We advise you begin looking for accommodation in London or Manchester as soon as possible. Although Arden does not offer university accommodation, we have partnered with trusted accommodation providers offering a variety of city-centre student housing options. Accommodation costs can vary, however private rentals can be in high competition. Learn more about accommodation Living expenses: Budget for essentials such as food, transport, and other daily costs. These living expenses also play a role in your visa application. Visa and immigration fees: These include the visa application fee and the immigration health surcharge, which grants you access to public healthcare in the UK. and funding Get a More Affordable Degree as an International Student Studying in the UK At Arden, we believe that everyone, everywhere has the right to higher education. We understand that studying abroad can bring additional financial challenges. That’s why we offer a range of scholarships and regional funding options designed specifically for international students. Arden UK Welcome Offer for International Students All International students studying in the UK will receive up to £5,000 fee reduction on their chosen course of study until September 2026. This means that students will pay: Course Fee Fee with offer - London Fee with offer - Manchester Undergraduate courses £16,000 £13,000 £12,000 Postgraduate courses (including MBAs) £17,500 £13,500 £12,500 Students studying in London or Manchester have the opportunity to achieve a high-quality degree for one of the lowest costs on the market for a short period only. Our degrees are industry focused, giving students the skills they need to progress their careers. Additionally, our degrees are accredited by organisations such as CMI, DMI, APM, and our Executive MBA was also ranked best MBA in the UK for the last two years running by CEO Magazine. These offers and scholarships allows you to put more of your funds to the cost of living whilst studying at Arden – giving you the peace of mind to focus on studying and experiencing life in the UK. Terms and conditions apply Arden University UK Offer for International Students Eligible international students studying at one of our UK campuses can receive a tuition fee reduction of up to £4,500 on their chosen course when they enrol for one of the following intakes: November 2026, February 2027 or May 2027. Course Fee Fee with offer - London Fee with offer - Manchester Undergraduate courses £16,000 £13,500 £12,500 Postgraduate courses (including MBAs) £17,500 £14,000 £13,000 Terms and conditions apply UK International Super Early Bird Offer International students studying at a UK campus could be eligible for a reduction of £3,000 from their Programme Fee for eligible programmes. This will depend on the receipt of an unconditional offer and deposit paid to Arden University by: 29th October 2026 for the November 2026 intake 25th January 2027 for the February 2027 intake, or; 12th April 2027 for the May 2027 intake. The UK International Super Early Bird Offer can be combined with any other offer, offered by Arden University. ( Terms and conditions apply . Valid until May 2027.) International Students Get a more affordable degree today, wherever you study from One of our core values at Arden is our belief that everyone, everywhere has the right to higher education. At the same time, we understand that money matters can be the biggest obstacle to completing a life-changing degree and achieving your full potential. That’s why we’ve set up a number of scholarships and regional offers to help students from across the globe earn the degree they’ve always wanted. Can I get a scholarship or regional offer? You can receive one regional offer per eligible programme you complete at Arden University, provided you meet our entry requirements and submit all the required documents. This discount will be applied to your tuition fees throughout your studies. Take a look below to explore our full range of university scholarships and regional offers, their requirements, and how you can get your application started today. International students studying online International students studying in the UK Arden University Alumni International students studying in Berlin Pakistani students International students studying online The Global Tier programme is an exclusive offer for online learners from selected international regions. This grants you access to Arden University's educational resources and support, nurturing your journey toward success. To qualify for the Global Tiers offer you must meet the following criteria: Region : You must be an international student that is a resident or national of one of the regions listed below. Eligibility requirements : please review our terms and conditions for detailed eligibility requirements. Application : You only need to apply to the course you’re interested in, from the selection below. Eligible Undergraduate degree courses (including Foundation Year and Top-ups) BA (Hons) Business Management (including Tourism, Accounting and Finance, Marketing, and Human Resource Management pathways) - (not including BA (Hons) Business Management Top-up) BSc (Hons) Accounting and Finance BSc (Hons) Psychology BSc (Hons) Psychology with Counselling LLB (Hons) Law BSc (Hons) Health and International students studying in the UK We have scholarships and funding offers available for international students studying at one of our UK campuses, in Manchester or London. For details visit the International Scholarships and Funding page . Arden University Alumni You could get 50% off tuition fees on a master’s course of your choice. This exclusive offer is available to all Arden University undergraduate alumni—whether you studied online, on campus in Berlin, or through blended learning in the UK. To qualify, you must: Have completed an Arden undergraduate degree with at least a 2:2 Meet the entry requirements for your chosen master’s course Apply within five years of graduating From MBAs to MScs, our postgraduate programmes are designed to help you move forward - whether you're changing careers, upskilling, or pursuing a lifelong passion. Our team can help you choose the right postgraduate path based on your goals. Find your postgraduate course Read our terms and conditions. International students studying in Berlin We offer a Berlin Regional Offer for international students coming to study in Berlin from eligible countries. To be eligible for this offer, you must meet the following criteria: Be a national of a country listed below at the date of your application (we reserve the right to request evidence of proof of nationality); and Have an offer to study your eligible programme (see below) for one of the following Berlin intakes: September 2026, November 2026, February 2027 or May 2027 The Regional Offer cannot be combined with any other offer run by us. If you are eligible for more than one offer, the offer that gives you the greatest discount will be applied. Countries eligible for Berlin Regional Offer South America Argentina Bolivia Brazil Chile Colombia Ecuador Paraguay Peru Uruguay North America USA Canada Central America El Salvador Guatemala Honduras Mexico Panama The Caribbean Anguilla Antigua and Barbuda Aruba Bahamas Barbados Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba Cayman Islands Cuba Curacao Dominica Dominican Republic Grenada Guadeloupe Haiti Jamaica Martinique Montserrat Netherlands Antilles Puerto Rico Saint Kitts and Nevis Saint Lucia Saint Martin Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Saint-Barthelemy MENA, Africa & CIS Region Algeria Armenia Azerbaijan Bahrain Botswana Cameroon Cote d’Ivoire Egypt Eritrea Ethiopia Gambia Georgia Ghana Jordan Kazakhstan Kenya Kuwait Kyrgyzstan Moldova Morocco Namibia Nigeria Oman Qatar Senegal Rwanda Saudi Arabia Sierra Leone Tajikistan Tanzania Turkey Turkmenistan UAE Uganda Uzbekistan Zambia South Asia Bangladesh Bhutan India Indonesia Nepal Pakistan Sri Lanka New September/November 2026 Only Countries Eligible countries only applicable to the September 2026 and November 2026 intakes Angola China Hong Kong Jamaica Japan Malaysia Myanmar* Philippines South Africa Taiwan Thailand Trinidad & Tobago Vietnam * Applicants from Myanmar must pay 100% of their tuition fees upfront as payment plans are not available for applicants from Myanmar. Receiving monies from Myanmar is also subject to approval from our Bank. If Bank approval is not given, you will not be eligible for this Regional Offer. Eligible programmes Master of Public Health MBA MSc Cyber Security MSc Data Science MSc Engineering Management MSc Project Management MSc Strategic Digital Marketing MSc Strategic Human Resource Management MSc Supply Chain Management and Logistics The Regional Offer fee reduction is dependent on intake. Please consider that this page only outlines a summary of the offer. Make sure to consult all our terms and conditions related to the Berlin Regional Offer before applying. Pakistani students studying in Berlin If your plans to study in the UK have changed due to visa restrictions, Arden University Berlin is here to help you keep moving forward. This offer is available to Pakistani nationals who have received, but not yet accepted, a conditional or unconditional offer or CAS from a UK university to study in person from 2026 onwards, and who choose to apply for an eligible Blended Learning programme at Arden University Berlin. The offer applies to eligible students starting their programme in September 2026, November 2026, or February 2027. To be eligible, students must: Be a Pakistani national Hold an offer or CAS from a UK university for 2026 entry Apply for an eligible blended learning programme at Arden University Berlin for a selected intake To be considered for this offer, please inform your recruitment advisor or agent during your application process and provide evidence confirming your eligibility. Financial Support – Terms and Conditions What is the Financial Support Bursary? The Financial Support Bursary (the “Bursary”) is available to students who are experiencing genuine and unforeseen financial hardship whilst at university, despite having applied for and received all other financial support. The Bursary can provide non-repayable grants towards essential living expenses and/or one-off unplanned costs and/or support for disability needs assessment. The Bursary can also help to provide essential IT equipment and short-term broadband connection for study. The Bursary cannot be used to fund the following: tuition fees - you must be in receipt of student finance or have a signed payment plan in place which covers your tuition fees. debts including gambling activities; or medium to long-term financial instability and shortfall. Not all Bursary awards may result in a cash payment. The University may distribute goods directly, for example a pre-approved laptop or a supermarket service voucher. Who is eligible? Please note that all awards are subject to eligibility checks. Submission of an application does not guarantee funding. To be eligible for this scheme, you must meet the following student requirements: be UK domiciled (with settled status where applicable) [applies to Financial Support Fund, Milestones/Emergency Fund, Digital Fund, DSA200, Commuter Travel Bursary, Pregnancy, Adoption and Family Leave Bursary, Care Experienced and Estranged Student Bursary, the Childcare Fund and the Graduation Fund]. OR be a registered and enrolled student at our Berlin Campus and domiciled in Germany [Berlin Financial Bursary] AND be facing financial hardship* have a household income of less than £35,000** be enrolled to any of Arden’s Undergraduate programmes. can demonstrate a shortfall in income versus expenditure which is contributing to financial hardship, such as an inability to meet living costs such as food, household bills, and/or travel*. be in receipt of the full Student Tuition Fee Loan to which you are entitled from the Student Loans Company or have entered into a registered payment plan with Arden University. be able to provide evidence of incomings and outgoings along with evidence of any dependents. where seeking funding for IT equipment, evidence of unaffordability. and confirmation that such equipment is not available via other grants and schemes such as the Disabled Students’ Allowance. be actively attending and engaged in your studies throughout the duration of the course. Attendance is defined as: presence at scheduled learning and teaching activities, including classes, workshops, and assessments. • Engagement is defined as: active participation in learning, including interaction with iLearn and other relevant virtual learning tools, timely submission of assessments, and responsiveness to university communication. *Does not apply to the DSA200 or Care Experienced/Estranged Student Bursary **Does not apply to the Childcare Fund which uses the Student Finance England criteria for household income of less than £20,107.23 if applying for one child and less than £28,914.47 household income if applying for more than one child in order to qualify for the Full time Childcare Grant. Students who are not eligible for the bursary are still encouraged to seek advice and guidance on debt and money from agencies such as Citizens Advice ( Debt and money - Citizens Advice ). You can also visit the Students’ Association Cost of Living Hub to find out about more external agencies or organisations that can provide you with tailored support. What evidence is required? Once your application has been received, we will request that you submit supporting documentary evidence to the Hardship Support Administration Team. The evidence required is dependent on your individual circumstances; details of required evidence will be provided to you. In addition to the standard evidence listed above, you may in some cases be asked to provide additional information. Bank Statements Please note that bank statements must be submitted as either a scan of the original document or in PDF format exported from your online banking or mobile banking app. You should submit bank statements that covers the month before the date of your application. The University has absolute discretion to request bank statements for up to three months before the date of your application. All bank statements should include any income and expenditure quoted in your application and should contain the following information: Your name and address. Your bank details, including sort code and account number. All transactions going into or out of accounts over £100/€100 should be annotated to explain the following: Where the transaction is from/to; and What the transaction is for. The University will not accept screenshots of your accounts or summaries detailed via any other format. Evidence must be provided for all accounts you hold, including any joint, savings, or ISA accounts. The University may recover funding in cases where students have withdrawn cash which cannot be evidenced with receipts as to what has been purchased with the sum withdrawn. Letters, tenancy agreements, and bills (e.g., Council Tax, utilities bills) Any documents submitted as evidence should be on company-headed paper, preferably displaying the organisation’s official stamp to show authenticity. Any evidence that contains a foreign language must be translated to English before submission to the University. In the case of tenancy documentation, you should inform the University of any debt/arrears regarding outstanding rent payments. Informal Rent/Board Family Arrangements In cases where you are paying rent or board to family members and there is evidence of regular payments via bank transfer, but no formal tenancy agreement is in place, you must provide the following evidence: A written statement or agreement confirming: The arrangement Payment amount Frequency of payments Three Bank statements evidencing the payments. Student Finance England Documentation (full-time undergraduate students only) You should evidence that you have been means-tested by Student Finance England (SFE). When submitting SFE evidence this must include all income including but not limited to maintenance loans, income from employment, and government benefits. Household income and Universal Credit If this is not shown on your recent bank statement, you may supply a P45 or P60 for the most recent tax year or a statement of earnings from HMRC. If your income was zero or you have an emergency tax code (e.g., ending in M1, W1, or T) you should submit a statement of earnings instead of a P60 (unless you are claiming one of the means-tested benefits listed below). For any additional income e.g., from external funding or government benefits please include a list of payments you have received and are yet to receive. If you receive Universal Credit, you will be asked to provide evidence such as your award letter; eligibility for Universal Credit is one of the factors we consider when assessing the validity of low-income status and requirement for financial support. Childcare costs You may be asked to provide evidence of invoices, outstanding childcare bills, and any correspondence regarding missed payments/debt arrears. For full-time students, you should also evidence why you have been assessed as not eligible for the childcare grant from SFE. How to apply? You must have a household income below £35,000 and be able to demonstrate financial hardship. You must be enrolled/active, have passed milestones and be regularly attending & engaging with your course. You must be in receipt of the maximum maintenance grant available from the Student Loans Company. You will only be considered for 1 award per 12-month period.

This fund is designed primarily to support students who require financial assistance during the milestones period of their course. The milestone period is defined as the first two weeks of an Arden University learner’s academic course and includes a series of mandatory components which must be completed in order to be registered as a learner. Payment of up to £200 is awarded depending on personal circumstances. Learners are able to access the emergency Fund following engagement with the Wellbeing Service, this is usually a one off payment.

To be eligible, you will need to meet the following criteria: You must be within your milestones period or in the event of a safeguarding response. You are registered and engaged with the Wellbeing Service around a Safeguarding concern. This will be awarded on a discretionary, case-by-case basis, taking into account a student’s individual circumstances. It is intended for situations where the student has no alternative means to obtain essential items or meet urgent needs deemed necessary by the safeguarding contact on duty.

A specified laptop will be awarded to you by the University. This does not include tablets, mobile phones, or any other digital equipment. A gift voucher for internet broadband will be awarded for a period of 3-months.

You must have a household income below £35,000 and be able to demonstrate financial hardship. You must be in continuous study for the duration of the course, defined as keeping a regular pattern of attendance, passed your milestones and submitting assessments on time. You need to exhaust all support available to you via the DSA £200 Laptop Contribution (https://www.blackbullion.com/funding/arden-university-inclusion-bursary) before applying to the Digital Fund. The laptop will include all essential software to complete your studies. You are not permitted to sell the laptop

If your award is successful, the supplier of the equipment in your DSA2 entitlement letter will be paid directly - no money will be paid directly to you. If you have not yet applied for DSA and need some support to do this, please contact the Wellbeing Team at: Wellbeing@arden.ac.uk
You may apply to the DSA (Disabled Students Allowance) £200 contribution Fund whilst waiting for the DSA200 letter from the DSA. Payment will be made upon receipt of the DSA200 entitlement letter.
Financial support in the form of a one-off payment of 200EU for essential food and travel.

You must be actively studying with a payment plan in place and be domiciled in Germany. You will be required to provide evidence of financial hardship. You are only eligible to apply or be granted this award once per year.
Up to 75% towards the cost of travel from home to Campus for students domiciled outside of a 3 mile radius.

You must have a household income below £35,000 and be able to demonstrate financial hardship. You must be enrolled and regularly attending & engaging with your course. You must live outside of a 3 mile radius from Campus and be able to provide evidence of travel to your campus including, if relevant, car parking charges .
BACS payment for: Up to £150 for travel, £33.60 for gown hire, £22.50 for a photo package.

You must have a household income below £35,000 and be able to demonstrate financial hardship. You must be enrolled on an undergraduate program at Arden University. You must have been invited to Graduation and attended to receive the award. Full criteria for the fund is contained within the Blackbullion Graduation Fund website.
Pregnancy, Adoption and Family Leave Bursary

You must have a household income below £35,000 and be able to demonstrate financial hardship You must be enrolled on an Arden University Blended Learning Programme and studying in the UK. You must be able to provide medical evidence of a birth, surrogacy, adoption, neonatal death, miscarriage or termination for you or your partner and be taking a Break in Learning due to this. You will be required to provide evidence of financial hardship. The Pregnancy, Adoption and Family Leave Bursary is provided on a first come first serve basis as funds are limited. To apply, you must be provided with a Blackbullion website link from the Wellbeing team following approval of your Break in Learning.
Care Experienced and Estranged Student Bursary

A bursary of £1,200 for full time and pro-rata for part time paid in two equal instalments each year of continuous study and regular attendance for a maximum of 4 years (£4,800) for BL and 8 years (£4,800) for DL programmes. Payments schedule for each intake will be: August intake (DL): October and April payments September intake : (BL): November and May payments October intake (DL) : January and July payments November intake (BL): February and July payments February intake (DL) : April and October payments February intake (BL): May and November April intake (DL): July and January May intake (BL): July and February A successful application for the Care Experienced and Estranged Student Bursary does not exclude the beneficiary from applying for other financial support funds. The Care experienced bursary budget is capped at £500,000

You must be a home student enrolled on a Blended Learning or Distance Learning undergraduate program. You must be paying full tuition fees in accordance with the published tuition fees. You must be in receipt of the maximum maintenance grant available to you from the Student Loans Company. You must be in continuous study for the duration of the course, defined as keeping a regular pattern of attendance, passed your milestones and submitting assessments on time. Care Experienced/Care Leavers You must have been care experienced in the UK at some stage in your life, and for any length of time, or been in care e.g. looked after by the local authority. This includes the following: spent time in the care of the local authority (e.g. foster care or children’s home) privately fostered. ‘looked after at home’ under a supervision order. in kinship foster care (where a friend or family member becomes the foster carer). kinship care through a formal arrangement, recognised by a Local Authority, and could be prior to a Special Guardianship Order. Evidence to support the application: You must provide evidence that you were in local authority care prior to starting your course. Care leaver evidence would normally be a letter from a Personal Adviser/After Care Social Worker; other forms of evidence may be accepted. Care-experienced. You will need to provide a letter on headed paper from the local authority where you spent time in care or with another official organisation who dealt with your care at the time it took place. This letter needs to confirm that you have spent time in care. Consideration will be given if you are care experienced but your personal circumstances do not meet the criteria outlined above. We reserve the right to make decisions regarding the allocation of funds under this bursary on a case-by-case basis. Estranged Students You will need to evidence that you are irreconcilably estranged your family or guardians. You have been assessed as independent by the Student Loan Company because you are estranged from your family or guardians or can provide evidence from a professional person who can confirm your estrangement. This can include a supporting letter from a solicitor, doctor, therapist, support worker, or tutor

Financial support for registered childcare costs The fund provides you with up to 15% of the childcare costs for pre school children dependent on the number of children in preschool childcare. If you are granted an award, we will require bank detail of the childcare provider to pay them directly as no payment will go directly to a student

You must be in receipt of the Full time Childcare Grant. (You must provide your Student Finance Entitlement Summary) You must be able to demonstrate unexpected financial hardship You are a current Arden University Blended Learning undergraduate and have completed and passed milestones. You can provide one month's recent bank statements (this is for your eligibility to be assessed) - Please note we may request additional bank statements. You are currently receiving the maximum student maintenance loan available to you (You must provide your Student Finance Entitlement Summary) You have not received an award from this fund in the last 12 months. You have not claimed for Childcare costs through the Financial Support Fund* Your childcare provider is on the Ofsted Early Years Register or General Childcare Register Each child you are claiming for is aged between 0-5 years old. You are not claiming the Childcare Element of Working Tax credits/Universal credits. *As a condition of this fund, you will not be eligible to claim childcare costs through the Financial Support Fund if you are successfully awarded the Childcare Fund In order to apply for the fund, you will need provide: A personal statement explaining the type of financial support you require along with the amounts. Evidence of financial hardship (supplied using one month's bank statements for all bank accounts) You must provide your Student Finance Entitlement Summary Childcare Ofsted approved on letterheaded paper Evidence that you have been awarded the 85% Childcare Grant by Student Finance England. Consent information Please note that by applying for the fund you are providing consent to personal information being provided to external suppliers. This is to arrange for access to your award. If you are not granted an award, this information will not be shared.

stored_scholarships.name: Arden University Regional Scholarship
stored_scholarships.requirements: Must be a resident of an eligible region (e.g. Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan); must apply for an undergraduate blended learning or online program; must demonstrate how the degree will benefit their local community in a 300-word statement.
stored_scholarships.description: Arden offers region-specific bursaries to support students from developing economies. This award reduces the 2026 tuition fees to make modern, flexible learning more affordable for international career-switchers.
